body:
The problem with dynamic strings is that they're effectively leaked, leading to an explosion of RAM use on many calls. At least, this was the case with tracy, which is why we needed to avoid their 'dynamic strings' API.
This has led to the (somewhat complicated) interning implementation found in the `.cpp`.

I strongly recommend testing if perfetto's implementation interns the strings automatically and handles complex loads well. If no, I recommend copying / abstracting the approach we took for tracy. Otherwise, you'll likely be limited to a few seconds of tracing in complex projects (as previous tests showed).

I tested by running Kenney's 3D Platformer for several tens of minutes (left the game running) and memory usage looked normal. I suspect this is due to a couple of reasons:
- From their documentation, perfetto seems to automatically interns the strings as mentioned in https://perfetto.dev/docs/instrumentation/track-events#interning
- perfetto provides an [in-process and system backends](https://perfetto.dev/docs/instrumentation/tracing-sdk#in-process-vs-system-mode) and we use the latter which means that the application only as a producer, connecting to the external traced daemon (system daemon)
If the backend is the system backend, did you check if memory accumulates elsewhere?

Didn't think to; I can reach out to the Google folks and check how to measure system backend memory growth but given that backend is built-in the Android OS and that it can handle profiling applications like Chrome, I'd expect it to be 'up to the task'.

I wouldn't be as sure; from my experience technology is often less 'prepared' than I'd hope :D

Anyway, thanks for testing. "Several tens of minutes" should be good enough. Let's leave the thread open in case anybody wants to chime in, but we can consider it resolved.

The current code allocates several strings at once (8 or so?). This could be a substantial burden on GDScript performance. Did you happen to test CPU impact of this change?

(This is also a problem that interning solves; but it should be possible to make it 'fast enough' even without it)

I'm open to suggestions to improve the current code. The macros are passed `StringName` arguments so I'm following the obvious approach to turning them into `String` in order to retrieve their data. 
Based on the [perfetto interning example](https://perfetto.dev/docs/instrumentation/track-events#interning), it looks like the same approach would be needed as well.

Well, it depends on if it's a bottleneck (would have to be measured). If yes, it's definitely worth fixing, and might block the PR for me. If not, we can ignore it. Somewhere in between, it needs a fix.
The best fix in this case would be either to intern the strings (would need multi-key lookup; not sure if feasible), or a bespoke string creator that allocates one buffer and fills it with contents rather than concatenating strings one by one (i planned to implement a generalized version of this some time, but never got around to it :/).

I recommend doing a quick profile run to see if the string allocations or general perfetto calls are having an impact.
I updated the format of the trace event name so the allocation of several strings at once is no longer an issue.
